title: BoolValue ≠ boolean
summary: BoolValue is an INSTANCE whose .Value is a boolean. Truthiness bites here: `if boolValue then` is ALWAYS truthy (it's an object!) — you must check boolValue.Value.

explanation.whatItIs: A double trap: wrapper objects plus Luau truthiness (only nil/false are falsy). A BoolValue is neither — it's an object, so it's truthy even when its Value is false.
explanation.whyItExists: Same reason all value objects exist: putting plain data in the tree. The confusion is the price.
symptoms: if flag then runs even when flag.Value == false
explanation.fix: Always compare the .Value: if flag.Value then. Same discipline as forgetting-dot-value.
tips: Modern alternative: instance attributes (flag:GetAttribute("IsOpen")) return real booleans
BoolValue.Changed passes the new boolean — handy for reactive systems
commonMistakes: Passing BoolValue objects where booleans are expected
not boolValue — still truthy object logic

examples.title: The trap
examples.code:
local isOpen = Instance.new("BoolValue")
isOpen.Value = false

if isOpen then
    print("This runs! isOpen is an object — truthy")
end

if isOpen.Value then
    print("This correctly does NOT run")
else
    print("False checked properly")
end
